preamble: The loss of the neutral central vowel /ə/, typically in unstressed syllables (syncope) or word-finally (apocope). It is one of the most frequent vowel deletions: English casual-speech syncope, the loss of Middle English final -e, French e muet, and Hindi schwa deletion all remove /ə/.

examples.note: Syncopated variant listed for General American, RP and other accents.
Final unstressed -e /ə/ was lost in late Middle English; the vowel change to /eɪ/ is the separate Great Vowel Shift.
Deletion of e muet (schwa) in the initial syllable; often written p'tit in familiar speech.
The inherent schwa is deleted medially and word-finally; likewise नमकीन is pronounced namkīn.
